title: Zhuan Launches Unified API for Claude and GPT at 75% Savings
summary: Zhuan offers a single API key for Claude and GPT models at approximately 25% of official pricing, simplifying multi-model integration for developers.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Zhuan launches a unified API service offering access to Claude and GPT models at approximately 25% of official pricing.
- Developers can switch between multiple foundation models using a single API key, eliminating the need for separate integrations.
- The platform aims to reduce infrastructure costs for AI applications while maintaining compatibility with existing model endpoints.


Zhuan has launched a unified API aggregator service that provides developers with access to both Claude and GPT models through a single[API key](https://emergent.sh/glossary/what-is-api-key) at approximately 75% lower costs than official pricing. Officially released on November 23, 2026, the platform addresses a persistent challenge in AI development: managing multiple API integrations while controlling infrastructure expenses.


## How the Unified API Works


The service consolidates access to multiple foundation models behind a single endpoint and authentication layer. Developers can switch between Claude variants from Anthropic and GPT models from OpenAI without maintaining separate API credentials or rewriting integration code. The platform handles routing, authentication, and rate limiting across provider boundaries, presenting a consistent interface regardless of the underlying model.


This approach simplifies the technical overhead for teams building AI-powered applications. Instead of managing multiple vendor relationships, billing accounts, and[API key rotation](https://emergent.sh/glossary/api-key-rotation) cycles, developers work with a single integration point. The service maintains compatibility with existing OpenAI and Anthropic SDKs by implementing drop-in replacement endpoints.


## Pricing Structure and Cost Savings


Zhuan claims to offer access at approximately 25% of official list prices, translating to roughly 75% savings on model inference costs. The pricing model appears to leverage volume purchasing, efficient routing, and potentially reserved capacity agreements with the foundation model providers. For high-volume applications processing millions of tokens daily, these cost reductions can represent substantial operational savings.


The economics are particularly compelling for startups and development teams running extensive testing, fine-tuning experiments, or serving cost-sensitive use cases. By reducing the per-token expense, the service lowers the barrier to experimenting with premium models like Claude Opus or GPT-6 variants that might otherwise exceed project budgets.


## Release Date and Availability


Officially launched on November 23, 2026, the service is immediately available to developers who sign up through the platform's website. The launch targets teams already using Claude or GPT APIs who seek cost optimization without sacrificing model quality or switching providers entirely.


Early access appears open to all registrants, though specific rate limits and tier structures have not been fully disclosed in the initial announcement. The platform likely operates on a usage-based billing model similar to the official APIs it aggregates.


## Technical Considerations


While the cost savings are significant, developers should evaluate several factors before migration. API aggregators introduce an additional layer between applications and foundation models, potentially affecting latency, uptime guarantees, and data handling policies. Teams working with sensitive data must verify that routing through a third-party service meets their compliance and security requirements.


The service's long-term viability depends on maintaining relationships with Anthropic and OpenAI, securing favorable pricing terms, and operating infrastructure at scale. Developers building production systems should assess vendor lock-in risks and ensure they can migrate back to direct API access if needed.


## What This Means


Zhuan's launch reflects growing demand for cost-effective access to frontier AI models as applications scale. By consolidating Claude and GPT behind a unified interface, the service addresses two pain points simultaneously: reducing complexity and lowering operational costs. For the broader AI development ecosystem, third-party aggregators like Zhuan may accelerate adoption of premium models by making them financially accessible to smaller teams and experimental projects. The launch also signals increasing commoditization of model access, where differentiation shifts from raw API availability to pricing, reliability, and developer experience.
